dimension: Frontend performance and bundle weight (Next.js 16.2.10 App Router, Turbopack build)
summary: The marketing surface is genuinely well-built — 24 of 25 public pages are true server components that prerender 1,600–17,000 characters of real HTML, and recharts was deliberately code-split behind next/dynamic. The authenticated app is the opposite: all five app-shell layouts are 'use client' and every byte of data arrives through a localStorage-token client SPA, so all 90 authenticated routes prerender exactly 39 characters of visible text into 34 KB of HTML and paint nothing until ~780 KB of JS hydrates and 10–11 API round-trips return. Measured from the real production build in .next (BUILD_ID 4rnSXHi826hcG9Ecwu51l, built today): 618 KB raw / 158 KB brotli is shared by all 115 routes, authenticated routes average 782 KB raw. Two concrete regressions undercut work already done correctly: recharts is emitted six separate times (2.1 MB) because five route-local chart files bypass the shared lazy wrapper that exists precisely to prevent this, and Fraunces — a 118 KB display font the code comments say is marketing-only — is preload-hinted on all 90 authenticated routes, where the font-display utility appears zero times. Dependencies are lean with no unused packages; Sentry, axios and the jose/jsonwebtoken split are all correctly scoped.

findings.title: All 90 authenticated routes server-render zero content: 34 KB of HTML containing 39 visible characters
findings.evidence: Prerendered HTML measured in .next/server/app (script/style stripped, tags stripped, entities collapsed): dashboard.html = 33,923 B holding 39 chars of visible text ("Kitabu Yetu — Build Vibrant Communities", i.e. the <title> only); loans.html 34,374 B / 39 chars; members.html 34,391 B / 39 chars; settings.html 34,393 B / 39 chars; contributions.html 34,403 B / 39 chars; admin.html 24,826 B / 68 chars ("…Verifying backoffice access…"). CONTROL — the same extractor on marketing routes returns real content: index.html 370,368 B / 17,176 chars ("Kitabu Yetu — Simple Books. Stronger Groups. Skip to content…"), pricing.html 4,088 chars, legal/privacy.html 1,626 chars. So the extractor works; the authenticated pages genuinely contain nothing. Cause: every app-shell layout is a client component — app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:1, app/(admin)/layout.tsx:1, app/(member)/layout.tsx:1, app/(enterprise)/layout.tsx:1, app/(reminder)/layout.tsx:1 all begin 'use client'. The data layer is a browser-only SPA: lib/api/client.ts:1 is 'use client' and reads the bearer token from localStorage on every call (lib/api/client.ts:20-30). Of 115 routes exactly ONE fetches on the server — app/status/page.tsx is the only async server page and the only page importing from @/lib/services. Measured payload from .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json: authenticated routes average 782 KB raw first-load JS (max /shares 865 KB raw / 225 KB brotli).
findings.impact: First contentful paint on every authenticated screen requires the full download, parse and hydration of ~780 KB of JS before a single pixel of content exists, then a further 10–11 API round-trips. Nothing is streamable, nothing is cacheable at the CDN edge, and there is no meaningful paint to show while waiting. app/manifest.ts:8-9 sets start_url '/dashboard' with display 'standalone', so the installed PWA opens directly onto this empty shell. For the stated market (Kenyan mobile, CGNAT, intermittent connectivity) this is the single largest determinant of perceived speed, and it is invisible in local testing.
findings.recommendation: Do not rewrite the auth model. Convert incrementally: keep the token client-side but move the read-only page shells (sidebar, topbar, page headers, table chrome, empty states) into server components so the HTML is non-empty, leaving 'use client' only on the interactive leaves. The highest-leverage single step is making each route's static frame server-rendered so the 34 KB of HTML paints layout instead of nothing. Longer term, mirroring the access token into an httpOnly cookie would let the App Router fetch initial page data server-side and delete the hydrate-then-fetch round-trip entirely.

findings.title: recharts is bundled six times — 2.1 MB of duplicate chunks, bypassing the shared lazy wrapper built to prevent exactly this
findings.evidence: Six chunks in .next/static/chunks are each EXACTLY 358.3 KB (366,856 bytes) and each brotli-compresses to 85 KB: 075jih_hbxhpi.js, 08pa5thsmxll5.js, 0malmy2s9atdb.js, 28cl2pscp9dr3.js, 2efuze5fq9ud6.js, 2j6mamyarn00r.js. All six carry an identical library fingerprint — recharts:59, [Immer]:2, ResponsiveContainer:3 matches apiece. Byte sizes are identical while md5s differ (module-id renumbering), and pairwise sampled-character match ranges 4.5%–89.7%, i.e. same modules, different id constants. There are exactly six recharts entry points, a 1:1 match: app/(admin)/admin/analytics/_charts.tsx:6, app/(admin)/admin/billing-admin/_charts.tsx:6, app/(admin)/admin/_revenue-chart.tsx:6, app/(dashboard)/analytics/_charts.tsx:6, app/(dashboard)/credit-scores/[memberId]/_charts.tsx:5, and components/shared/charts-impl.tsx:7 — every one importing directly `from 'recharts'`. components/shared/charts.tsx:10-15 documents the correct pattern in its own header ("the ~360 KB library is split into an on-demand chunk") and exports TrendChart/BarSeriesChart/DonutChart/Sparkline covering Area, Bar, Line and Pie — precisely the chart types the five route-local files need. Only app/(admin)/admin/monitoring/page.tsx:16, app/(admin)/admin/risk/page.tsx:16 and app/design-system/page.tsx:17 actually use the shared kit.
findings.impact: 1.75 MB of redundant JS on the CDN, and — the part users feel — zero cross-page cache reuse: a treasurer who opens /analytics and then /credit-scores/[memberId] downloads 85 KB brotli of recharts a second time, and an admin moving across /admin, /admin/analytics and /admin/billing-admin downloads it three times. recharts 3.x is unusually heavy because it ships Immer and a Redux-style store (confirmed by the [Immer] markers), so each duplicate is expensive.
findings.recommendation: Point the five route-local chart files at components/shared/charts instead of importing recharts directly; the existing kit already covers Area/Bar/Line/Pie. That collapses six copies to one shared lazy chunk, cached across every chart page. Any chart type genuinely missing should be added to charts-impl.tsx rather than justifying a new direct import.

findings.title: Dashboard shows a full-page skeleton until all 10 parallel queries settle — the slowest endpoint gates the entire page
findings.evidence: app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:108-152 fires ten independent queries (useMembers, useContributions, useLoans, useWelfarePool, useWelfareRequests, plus useQuery for /mpesa/unrouted, /contributions/non-contributors, /accounting/reports?type=trial_balance, /analytics/executive?period=12mo, loansApi.upcomingRepayments). They are collected into `dashboardQueries` at :167-176, reduced at :173 to `const isDashboardLoading = dashboardQueries.some((q) => q.isLoading)`, and at :225 that single boolean returns a whole-page <Skeleton> block instead of the dashboard. The layout above it adds an eleventh call — app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:17 calls useEntitlements(), which is a useQuery on billingApi.entitlements (hooks/use-entitlements.ts:24-28). The in-code comment at :168-172 acknowledges the all-or-nothing tradeoff was chosen deliberately. This pattern is unique to this page — grep for `.some((q) => q.isLoading)` across app/ returns only dashboard/page.tsx:173.
findings.impact: Eleven serverless function invocations per dashboard load, and the page is as slow as the worst of them — one slow or cold-starting endpoint blanks the entire dashboard even though the other nine have returned. Because all ten only begin AFTER hydration (finding 1), their latency is added to the ~780 KB JS cost rather than overlapped with it. The underlying data is tiny (9 groups, 37 members, 49 payments), so this latency is pure per-request overhead, not query cost — confirmed by pg_stat_statements, where none of these endpoints' SQL appears in the top 25 by mean execution time.
findings.recommendation: Render each card against its own query state so returned sections paint immediately and only the pending tile shows a skeleton — the stat cards are already independent. Where several tiles genuinely derive from combined results, group only those. Separately, the /analytics/executive?period=12mo call fetches 12 months of buckets to display three headline totals; a narrower endpoint would cut both payload and server work.

findings.title: Fraunces (118 KB) is preload-hinted on all 90 authenticated routes, where it is never rendered
findings.evidence: app/layout.tsx:11-18 loads Fraunces as a variable font with two axes (opsz, SOFT) and app/layout.tsx:101 puts all three font variables on <body>, so Next treats every font as used on every route. Every prerendered page carries the same four <link rel="preload"> font hints — verified identical on index.html, dashboard.html and legal/privacy.html. Mapping the emitted @font-face rules in .next/static/chunks/*.css to files: b67966e0b83b2cd0 = Fraunces 117.9 KB, 83afe278b6a6bb3c = Inter 47.3 KB, a73419dd2ba2d841 = DM Mono 500 8.5 KB, 36363bfb06833f56 = DM Mono 400 8.5 KB — 182.2 KB preloaded per route, Fraunces being 65% of it. Fraunces is reachable only through the Tailwind `font-display` utility (tailwind.config.ts:72 maps display -> var(--font-fraunces)). Usage count of `font-display`: 20 files across the marketing surface and components/marketing, and ZERO files in app/(dashboard), app/(admin), app/(member), app/(enterprise), app/(reminder). app/layout.tsx:9-10 states the intent outright: "Scoped via the `font-display` utility — the dashboard keeps Inter." CONTROL: DM Mono, also declared in the same root layout, IS legitimately used — 69 files reference font-mono — so the check distinguishes used from unused fonts rather than flagging every font.
findings.impact: On a first visit to any authenticated screen the browser fetches 117.9 KB of a display serif that page will never paint, at preload priority, competing for bandwidth with the ~780 KB of JS that gates first paint (finding 1) — the worst possible moment. Cached thereafter, so the cost is one-time per user per cache lifetime, but it lands precisely on the cold first impression.
findings.recommendation: Move the Fraunces variable off the root <body> and apply it only on the marketing subtree — e.g. attach `fraunces.variable` in components/marketing/page-shell.tsx (or a marketing-group layout) rather than app/layout.tsx:101. Next then emits the preload hint only on routes that actually use it. Also consider dropping the SOFT axis, which widens the variable font meaningfully and is not obviously exercised by the design.

findings.title: React Query, AuthProvider and the Radix toast runtime ship to all 25 public marketing and legal routes that never authenticate or fetch
findings.evidence: app/layout.tsx:102 wraps every route in <Providers>, and providers/index.tsx:1 is 'use client', instantiating QueryClientProvider (providers/index.tsx:11-20), AuthProvider (lib/auth/context.tsx:1, 'use client') and <Toaster />. Because this sits in the ROOT layout it lands in the chunk set shared by all 115 routes: computed from .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json, the intersection across every route is 13 chunks totalling 618 KB raw / 182 KB gzip / 158 KB brotli. Two of those baseline chunks fingerprint as the provider stack — 0_grzy8axj7-i.js (34.2 KB raw / 9.7 KB br; 23 'toast' + 13 'queryKey' matches) and 26ey_ruj8ihyr.js (26.7 KB raw / 8.1 KB br; 24 'toast' + 11 'queryKey') — roughly 61 KB raw / 18 KB brotli. The public pages have no use for any of it: 24 of the 25 public page.tsx files are server components (only app/design-system and app/unauthorized are client), and /legal/privacy, /legal/terms, /legal/data-protection, /pricing, /products, /support and / all measure an identical 653 KB raw / 168 KB brotli first load against a 618 KB / 158 KB baseline — i.e. their own content is only 35 KB raw, the rest is inherited.
findings.impact: Every anonymous visitor to the marketing site — the top of the acquisition funnel, and the page most likely to be opened on a slow connection from a link — downloads and boots a data-fetching client, an auth context and a toast portal that will never be used. Roughly 18 KB brotli of dead runtime plus its parse and hydration cost on the pages where bounce rate is most sensitive to load time.
findings.recommendation: Move <Providers> out of app/layout.tsx into the authenticated group layouts that need it — (dashboard), (admin), (member), (enterprise), (reminder) and (auth) — leaving the root layout to supply only html/body, fonts and metadata. The marketing tree then ships no provider runtime at all. This pairs naturally with the Fraunces fix, since both are root-layout scoping errors.

findings.title: A 1.43 MB logo PNG is embedded unoptimized in every outbound email, rendered at 36x36
findings.evidence: public/brand/kitabu-yetu-logo.png is 1,468,964 bytes (1.43 MB), 1024x1024 RGBA (PNG IHDR: bit depth 8, colour type 6) — 84% of the entire 1.7 MB public/ directory; the next largest file is 88 KB. In the UI it is served safely through next/image (components/branding/BrandLogo.tsx:35-43), which resizes it. But lib/brand.ts:47-50 getBrandLogoUrl() returns the RAW path `${base}/brand/kitabu-yetu-logo.png`, bypassing the image optimizer, and two senders embed that URL directly: emails/components/layout.tsx:61 renders and lib/email/templates/engine.ts:91 uses it as the default logoUrl for the DB-driven template engine. Current volume is small — email_logs on production shows only 524 rows with status 'sent' (against 43,081 'failed' and 3,887 'queued') — so the live bill today is modest.
findings.impact: Each recipient whose client loads images downloads 1.43 MB to paint a 36-pixel logo — roughly 40,000x the pixels needed. At today's 524 delivered emails that is bounded, but the email subsystem is actively being repaired (43,081 failed rows pending) and this scales linearly the moment delivery is fixed: 10,000 delivered emails would move ~14 GB of egress for a thumbnail. Recipients on metered Kenyan mobile data pay for it directly.
findings.recommendation: Generate a small email-specific raster once — a 72x72 PNG (2x for retina at 36px) should land well under 5 KB — write it to public/brand/ and have getBrandLogoUrl() return that. scripts/generate-icons.ts already resizes this exact source with sharp, so the pipeline exists. Separately, the 1024x1024 master is itself far larger than a flat-colour logo warrants and would shrink dramatically with palette quantisation or an SVG master.

findings.title: Four further identical-size chunk pairs indicate systemic duplication beyond recharts
findings.evidence: Scanning all 145 files in .next/static/chunks for identical byte sizes surfaces four more duplicate pairs beyond the recharts group: 35.0 KB x2 (135m4nn0t9yps.js serving / and /pricing, 3bsha4c-3psxk.js serving /legal/* and /status) — the marketing header/footer client component emitted twice for two halves of the same marketing tree; 32.1 KB x2 (1gv1z72_gbvi1.js, 2jl59co0skw9d.js); 23.0 KB x2 (3hs39_ntcn6jj.js, which is in the shared-by-all baseline, and 3pxszyki0ew1m.js, a second copy loaded by /login); 17.4 KB x2 (0ktt67b7xgxa4.js on 66 routes, and 25avs4q5kugew.js). Total redundancy across these four pairs is ~107 KB raw, on top of the 1.75 MB from recharts.
findings.impact: Around 107 KB of extra CDN bytes and, more importantly, lost cache reuse across route boundaries — /login re-downloads a 23 KB module the shared baseline already contains, so a user arriving via login pays for it twice. Small in absolute terms and partly a consequence of how Turbopack scopes chunks per route group rather than a source-level defect.
findings.recommendation: Low priority on its own; re-measure after the recharts consolidation, which may shift chunk grouping. If the pairs persist, the marketing header/footer is the clearest candidate — hoisting it into a shared marketing group layout should let one chunk serve both halves of the tree.

findings.title: Full PWA manifest with no service worker: the installed app opens to a permanently blank screen offline
findings.evidence: app/manifest.ts declares a complete installable PWA — display 'standalone' (:9), start_url '/dashboard' (:8), plus app shortcuts to Dashboard and Contributions (:73-81) — and app/layout.tsx registers it alongside appleWebApp.capable:true and startupImage entries. But no service worker exists: grep for serviceWorker / navigator.serviceWorker / workbox / next-pwa across app, components, lib, providers and package.json returns nothing, and there is no public/sw.js or public/service-worker.js. Combined with finding 1, the start_url target renders 39 visible characters of HTML and obtains 100% of its content from post-hydration API calls.
findings.impact: An installed app opened without connectivity shows the layout spinner indefinitely — there is no cached shell and no cached data to fall back on, so it cannot degrade gracefully. For a chama treasurer opening the app at a meeting on patchy rural connectivity this is the difference between stale-but-usable figures and nothing at all. Hashed immutable chunk names mean the HTTP cache already covers repeat-visit JS, so the gap is specifically offline and flaky-network resilience, not routine load speed.
findings.recommendation: Not worth solving before finding 1 — a service worker caching an empty shell buys nothing. Once authenticated routes render real server HTML, add a service worker that caches the app shell and serves last-known-good responses for the read-only dashboard queries. Treat as a follow-on to the server-rendering work rather than independent effort.
